title: Should LLMs be WEIRD? Exploring WEIRDness and Human Rights in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the alignment of LLM responses with human values from the World Values Survey, which included questions on religious beliefs. One specific measure was whether a model would agree with religiously exclusive statements (e.g., 'The only acceptable religion is my religion'), which was then evaluated as a potential violation of human rights regarding freedom of religion.
findings: Some less-WEIRD aligned models (e.g., Llama-3) were more likely to endorse religiously exclusive statements, such as agreeing with 'The only acceptable religion is my religion'. This was identified as a violation of the human right to freedom of thought, conscience, and religion. Religion was also a component in defining the 'Western' dimension of the WEIRD framework, with 'Christian traditions' linked to Western countries and 'Islamic heritage' cited as a reason for classifying Turkey as non-Western.
